title: Total influence as the sum of coordinate influences
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function, and for each coordinate $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$ let $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \E\!\left[(f(x)-f(x^i))^2/4\right]$ denote the influence of coordinate $i$, where $x^i$ is $x$ with its $i$-th bit flipped and $\E$ is expectation under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. Then the total influence of $f$ is the sum of the individual coordinate influences,
\[
  I[f] \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{n} \mathrm{Inf}_i[f].
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n
replaced:
The total influence is the sum of the coordinate influences:
$I[f] = \sum_{i} \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$.
